source_text: CUM moneat Dominus et dicat: Vos estis sal terrae, cumque esse nos jubeat ad innocentiam simplices, et tamen cum simplicitate prudentes, quid aliud, fratres dilectissimi, quam providere nos convenit, et sollicito corde vigilantes, subdoli hostis insidias intelligere pariter et cavere ne qui Christum sapientiam Dei Patris induimus, minus sapere in tuenda salute videamur? Neque enim persecutio sola metuenda est et ea quae subruendis ac dejiciendis Dei servis aperta impugnatione grassantur. Facilior cautio est ubi manifesta formido est, et ad certamen animus ante praestruitur quando se adversarius confitetur. Plus metuendus est et cavendus inimicus cum latenter obrepit, cum, per pacis imaginem fallens, occultis accessibus serpit; unde et nomen serpentis accepit. Ea est ejus semper astutia, ea est circumveniendi hominis caeca et latebrosa fallacia. Sic ab initio statim mundi fefellit, et, verbis mendacibus blandiens, rudes animas incauta credulitate decepit. Dominum ipsum tentare conatus, quasi obreperet rursus et falleret, latenter accessit. Intellectus tamen est et retusus; et ideo prostratus, quia agnitus atque detectus. Unde nobis exemplum datum est veteris hominis viam fugere, vestigiis Christi viventis insistere; ne denuo incauti in mortis laqueum revolvamur, sed, ad periculum providi, accepta immortalitate potiamur. Immortalitate autem potiri quomodo possumus, nisi ea quibus mors expugnatur et vincitur, Christi mandata servemus, ipso monente et dicente: Si vis ad vitam venire, serva mandata. Et iterum: Si feceritis quae mando vobis, jam non dico vos servos, sed amicos. Hos denique fortes dicit et stabiles, hos super petram robusta mole fundatos, hos contra omnes tempestates et turbines saeculi immobili et inconcussa firmitate solidatos. Qui audit, inquit, verba mea et facit ea, similabo eum viro sapienti qui aedificavit domum suam supra petram. Descendit pluvia, venerunt flumina, flaverunt venti et impegerunt in domum illam, et non cecidit; fundata enim fuit super petram. Verbis igitur ejus insistere, quaecumque et docuit et fecit discere et facere debemus. Caeterum credere se in Christum, quomodo dicit qui non facit quod Christus facere praecepit? Aut unde perveniet ad praemium fidei, qui fidem non vult servare mandati? Nutet necesse est et vagetur, et, spiritu erroris abreptus, velut pulvis quem ventus excutit ventiletur; nec ambulando proficiet ad salutem, qui salutaris viae non tenet veritatem. Cavenda sunt autem, fratres dilectissimi, non solum quae sunt aperta atque manifesta, sed et astutae fraudis subtilitate fallentia. Quid vero astutius, quidve subtilius, quam ut Christi adventu detectus ac prostratus inimicus, postquam lux Gentibus venit et sospitandis hominibus salutare lumen effulsit, ut surdi auditum gratiae spiritalis admitterent, aperirent ad Deum oculos suos caeci, infirmi aeterna sanitate revalescerent, claudi ad Ecclesiam currerent, muti claris vocibus et precibus orarent, videns ille idola derelicta et per nimium credentium populum sedes suas ac templa deserta, excogitaverit novam fraudem, ut sub ipso christiani nominis titulo fallat incautos? Haereses invenit et schismata, quibus subverteret fidem, veritatem corrumperet, scinderet unitatem. Quos detinere non potest in viae veteris caecitate, circumscribit et decipit novi itineris errore. Rapit de ipsa Ecclesia homines; et, dum sibi appropinquasse jam lumini atque evasisse saeculi noctem videntur, alias nescientibus tenebras rursus infundit, ut cum Evangelio Christi et cum observatione ejus et lege non stantes, Christianos se vocent, et ambulantes in tenebris habere se lumen existiment, blandiente adversario atque fallente, qui, secundum Apostoli vocem, transfigurat se velut angelum lucis, et ministros suos subornat velut ministros justitiae, asserentes noctem pro die, interitum pro salute, desperationem sub obtentu spei, perfidiam sub praetextu fidei, antichristum sub vocabulo Christi; ut, dum verisimilia mentiuntur, veritatem subtilitate frustrentur. Hoc eo fit, fratres dilectissimi, dum ad veritatis originem non reditur, nec caput quaeritur, nec magistri coelestis doctrina servatur.
thought_title: Warning Against the Wiles of the Enemy
pass_a_gloss: When the Lord warns and says: You are the salt of the earth, and since He commands us to be simple in innocence, and yet prudent with simplicity, what else is fitting for us, most beloved brothers, than to be provident and, with a solicitous heart being vigilant, to understand and equally beware of the insidious plots of the cunning enemy, lest we, who have put on Christ, the wisdom of God the Father, seem to be less wise in guarding our salvation? For it is not only persecution that is to be feared, and those things that openly attack and overthrow the servants of God. Caution is easier where there is manifest fear, and the mind is prepared for battle when the adversary confesses himself. The enemy is more to be feared and avoided when he creeps in secretly, when, deceiving by the image of peace, he slips in with hidden approaches; whence he has also received the name of serpent. This is always his cunning, this is the blind and hidden deceit of circumventing man. Thus from the beginning of the world he deceived, and, flattering with lying words, he deceived rude souls with unguarded credulity. He even tried to tempt the Lord Himself, and, as if he would creep in again and deceive, he approached secretly. However, he was understood and repulsed; and therefore he was prostrated, because he was recognized and detected. Whence an example has been given to us to flee the way of the old man, to follow in the footsteps of the living Christ; lest, being unguarded, we again fall into the snare of death, but, being provident of the danger, we may attain immortality. But how can we attain immortality, unless we keep the commandments of Christ, by which death is overcome and conquered, He Himself warning and saying: If you wish to come to life, keep the commandments. And again: If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants, but friends. These, finally, He calls strong and stable, founded on a strong rock, solidified with immovable and unshakable firmness against all the tempests and whirlwinds of the world. He who hears, He says, my words and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on a rock. The rain came down, the rivers came, the winds blew and struck that house, and it did not fall; for it was founded on a rock. Therefore, we must insist on His words, and do and learn what He has taught. But how can one believe himself to be in Christ, who does not do what Christ has commanded to be done? Or whence will he come to the reward of faith, who does not wish to keep the faith of the commandment? It is necessary that he waver and wander, and, seized by the spirit of error, be blown about like dust which the wind blows; nor will he make progress towards salvation, who does not hold to the truth of the salutary way. But we must beware, most beloved brothers, not only of those things that are open and manifest, but also of the subtle deceit of hidden fraud. What, indeed, is more cunning, what more subtle, than that the enemy, detected and prostrated by the advent of Christ, after the light has come to the Gentiles and the salutary light has shone for the salvation of men, that the deaf might receive the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind might open their eyes to God, the weak might be strengthened by eternal health, the lame might run to the Church, the mute might pray with clear voices and prayers, seeing that idols have been abandoned and his seats and temples have been deserted by the multitude of believers, has devised a new fraud, that he might deceive the unguarded under the very title of the Christian name? He has invented heresies and schisms, by which he might subvert the faith, corrupt the truth, and divide the unity. Those whom he cannot detain in the blindness of the old way, he surrounds and deceives with the error of the new way. He snatches men from the very Church; and, while they seem to have approached the light and escaped the night of the world, he pours darkness into them again, unaware, so that, not standing with the Gospel of Christ and with its observation and law, they call themselves Christians, and, walking in darkness, think they have the light, the adversary flattering and deceiving, who, according to the voice of the Apostle, transforms himself into an angel of light, and his ministers into ministers of justice, asserting night for day, destruction for salvation, desperation under the pretext of hope, perfidy under the pretext of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ; so that, while they speak what is plausible, they may frustrate the truth with subtlety. This happens, most beloved brothers, while we do not return to the origin of truth, nor seek the head, nor preserve the doctrine of the heavenly Master.

choices.why: The Latin phrase 'subdoli hostis' is more accurately translated as 'cunning enemy' to convey the sense of deceit and stealth.
The Latin phrase 'astutae fraudis' is more accurately translated as 'subtle deceit of hidden fraud' to convey the sense of cunning and stealth.
The Latin phrase 'veritatis originem' is more accurately translated as 'origin of truth' to convey the sense of the source or beginning of truth.

pass_b_english: When the Lord warns us, saying, "You are the salt of the earth" (Matt. 5:13), and commands us to be simple in innocence yet prudent with simplicity, what else is fitting for us, most beloved brothers, than to be provident and, with a solicitous heart, vigilant — to understand and equally beware the cunning enemy's insidious plots, lest we who have put on Christ, the wisdom of God the Father, seem less wise in guarding our salvation? For it is not only persecution that is to be feared, nor only those things that openly attack and overthrow the servants of God. Caution is easier where fear is manifest, and the mind prepares for battle when the adversary shows himself. The enemy is more to be feared and avoided when he creeps in secretly, deceiving by the image of peace and slipping in by hidden approaches — which is why he has also received the name of serpent. This is always his cunning, this the blind and hidden deceit of circumventing man. Thus from the beginning of the world he deceived, and, flattering with lying words, he deceived rude souls with unguarded credulity. He even tried to tempt the Lord Himself, approaching secretly as if to creep in again and deceive; but he was understood and repulsed, and therefore prostrated, because he was recognized and detected. From this an example has been given us: to flee the way of the old man and follow in the footsteps of the living Christ, lest, being unguarded, we fall again into the snare of death, but, being provident of the danger, we may attain immortality. Yet how can we attain immortality unless we keep the commandments of Christ, by which death is overcome and conquered — He Himself warning and saying, "If you wish to come to life, keep the commandments" (John 14:15), and again, "If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants, but friends"? These, finally, He calls strong and stable, founded on a strong rock, solidified with immovable and unshakable firmness against all the tempests and whirlwinds of the world. "He who hears my words and does them," He says, "I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on a rock. The rain came down, the rivers came, the winds blew and struck that house, and it did not fall; for it was founded on a rock" (Matt. 7:24-27). Therefore we must insist on His words, and learn and do whatever He has taught and done. But how can one believe himself to be in Christ who does not do what Christ commanded? Or whence will he come to the reward of faith who does not wish to keep the faith of the commandment? He must waver and wander, and, seized by the spirit of error, be blown about like dust which the wind blows; nor will he make progress toward salvation who does not hold to the truth of the salutary way. But we must beware, most beloved brothers, not only of those things that are open and manifest, but also of those that deceive by the subtle deceit of hidden fraud. What indeed is more cunning, what more subtle, than that the enemy — detected and prostrated by the advent of Christ, after the light has come to the Gentiles and the salutary light has shone for the salvation of men, that the deaf might receive the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind might open their eyes to God, the weak might be strengthened by eternal health, the lame might run to the Church, the mute might pray with clear voices and prayers, seeing that idols have been abandoned and his seats and temples deserted by the multitude of believers — has devised a new fraud to deceive the unguarded under the very title of the Christian name? He has invented heresies and schisms by which to subvert the faith, corrupt the truth, and divide the unity. Those whom he cannot detain in the blindness of the old way, he surrounds and deceives with the error of the new way. He snatches men from the very Church; and while they seem to have approached the light and escaped the night of the world, he pours darkness into them again, unaware, so that, not standing with the Gospel of Christ and with its observance and law, they call themselves Christians, and, walking in darkness, think they have the light — the adversary flattering and deceiving, who, according to the voice of the Apostle, transforms himself into an angel of light, and his ministers into ministers of justice, asserting night for day, destruction for salvation, desperation under the pretext of hope, perfidy under the pretext of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ (2 Cor. 11:14-15); so that, while they speak what is plausible, they may frustrate the truth with subtlety. This happens, most beloved brothers, while we do not return to the origin of truth, nor seek the head, nor preserve the doctrine of the heavenly Master.
